dct_description_sm: Yukon Government's (YG) climate change adaptation efforts began formally in 2009 with the Yukon Government Climate Change Action Plan and a clear articulation of adaptation as a key government priority. With the addition of Aboriginal Affairs and Northern Development Canada (AANDC), Northern Strategy Trust Fund, and other partnerships, YG was able to mobilize key adaptation projects across the territory. The overall intent was that effective climate change adaptation projects become mainstream activity for YG departments and the communities they affect thereby offering effective climate change adaptation approaches to all Yukoners. The Yukon Government chose Yukon's best proposals for adaptation projects and put them forth when applying for AANDC funding. This particular project dealt with the fact that the current national agriculture capability system, which quantifies an area's agricultural potential, does not identify key permafrost indicators nor take into account the effects of changing permafrost conditions on agriculture capability. The goal was to identify challenges to agriculture on areas of changing permafrost, develop best management practices for agriculture production in such areas, and examine the vulnerability of the national agriculture capability classification systems to changing permafrost conditions. Applying the information to the national agriculture capability ratings would increase the accuracy and consistency of the classification system for affected Yukon permafrost areas.
dct_subject_sm: Social sciences, economics and policy -> Adaptation
dct_title_s: Effects of changing permafrost conditions on agriculture and agriculture capability classification in Yukon
